```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 110,
                      eval = requireNamespace("cluster", quietly = TRUE) &&
                        requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE))
library(cpueTargeting)
library(ggplot2)
```

This example applies the toolbox to a simulated logbook that looks like real
data: ten species, three fishing tactics, trips that combine two sets,
rounding, under-reporting, a species recorded under two names, missing and
coarse positions, fleet turnover and a closure. Because the data are
simulated, the true tactics and the true biomass trends are known, so every
step can be checked.

Three species show three typical situations, each in its own section:

| Species | Habitat and gear | Situation |
|---|---|---|
| **Blackspot seabream** | deep reef, reef handline | demersal target; remove the pelagic trips, then standardise |
| **Conger** | reef at all depths, caught by both bottom gears | define indicator vessels by rules; choose the error distribution |
| **Dolphinfish** | seasonal pelagic migrant, trolling | keep only pelagic trips; seasonality in zeros and catch rates |

How the simulator works and what the PCs and clusters capture is shown in
*Setting up the logbook simulator: a user guide*; the general steps are
explained in *Analysing real catch and effort data: a step-by-step guide*.

# The logbook

```{r simulate}
sim <- simulate_logbook(seed = 1)
sp_tab <- sim$settings$species
knitr::kable(sp_tab[, c("species", "group", "habitat", "depth_mu", "price")],
             row.names = FALSE)
```

Nominal CPUE (orange) against the true biomass (black):

```{r om-cpue, fig.height = 5}
sim$Plots$cpue
```

This is what an analyst receives; the tactic is not in the logbook:

```{r logbook}
head(sim$logbook, 8)
```

# Common steps: format, fleet and species

```{r format}
x <- cpue_data(sim$logbook, year = "year", species = "species", catch = "kg",
               effort = "hours", id = "trip", vessel = "vessel",
               lon = "lon", lat = "lat", covariates = "month",
               synonyms = c("Blackspot seabream" = "Pagellus bogaraveo"))
x <- subset(x, !is.na(lon), note = "positions reported")
targets <- c("Pagellus bogaraveo", "Conger conger", "Coryphaena hippurus")
x <- select_species(x, threshold = 0.95, keep = targets)
x
```

```{r fleet, fig.height = 5}
fl <- plot_fleet(x)
fl$vessels
```

Species groups for the selection steps below (only species that are still in
the data):

```{r groups}
demersal <- intersect(sp_tab$species[sp_tab$group == "demersal"], x$species_labels)
pelagic <- intersect(sp_tab$species[sp_tab$group == "pelagic"], x$species_labels)
x0 <- x            # before targeting covariates, used for the conger section
```

# Targeting covariates for the whole fleet

```{r targeting}
x <- add_targeting(x)
plot_oc(x)
tactic_table(x)
```

```{r targeting-plots, fig.height = 5}
plot_biplot(x)
pt <- plot_targeting(x, res = 0.5)
pt$time
pt$pcs_time
```

Across the whole fleet, the first axis is typically dominated by the
contrast between pelagic and demersal trips (check the loadings). For a demersal species, that contrast is mostly
noise: the relevant targeting is *within* the demersal trips (reef or
sediment, shallow or deep). This is why the species sections below first
select the relevant tactics and then recompute the PCA.

```{r helper}
# relative indices of several fits against the truth
compare_indices <- function(fits, true) {
  idx <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(n) {
    i <- cpue_index(fits[[n]]$fit, fits[[n]]$model)
    data.frame(year = i$year, relative = i$relative, lower = i$lower,
               upper = i$upper, index = n)
  }))
  true$true <- true$true / mean(true$true)
  ggplot(idx, aes(x = year, y = relative, colour = index, fill = index)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_line(data = true, aes(x = year, y = true), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              colour = "black", linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 3) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Relative CPUE", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
         subtitle = "black: true biomass") + theme_bw()
}
```

# Blackspot seabream (deep reef)

Blackspot seabream lives on deep reefs and is caught mainly by the reef
handline. Its price is high in 2000-2007; during the pelagic boom
(2008-2015) much of the fleet trolls for pelagic species instead.

## Remove the pelagic trips and recompute the PCA

`select_tactics()` keeps the clusters whose catch is at least 50% demersal
species and reruns `add_targeting()` on the remaining trips.

```{r sbr-select}
xd <- select_tactics(x, species = demersal, min_share = 0.5)
xd$targeting$previous$share          # demersal share of each previous cluster
tactic_table(xd)
tail(xd$log, 3)
```

```{r sbr-biplot, fig.height = 5}
plot_biplot(xd)
```

The new PCs describe the demersal targeting, e.g. reef against sediment
species and shallow against deep (check the loadings).

> **Guidelines: selecting tactics**
>
> * Select on a **group of species** (here all demersal species), not on the
>   target alone. Clusters are derived from the catch composition; keeping
>   only clusters rich in the target would select trips by their catch of
>   the target, and part of its abundance signal with them.
> * Check `xd$targeting$previous$share`: the removed clusters should be
>   clearly different (here almost no demersal catch), not borderline.
> * Mixed trips (two tactics in one record) fall between clusters; some are
>   removed with the pelagic cluster. Check the share removed by year
>   (`plot_targeting(x)$time` before the selection): a trend means the
>   selection itself follows the targeting.
> * Compare the index with and without the selection.

## Standardise

```{r sbr-fit}
fit_sbr <- fit_cpue(xd, species = "Pagellus bogaraveo",
                    models = c("Base", "Base+S", "Cluster+S", "DPC+S"),
                    vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
cpue_diagnostics(fit_sbr)
```

```{r sbr-index, fig.height = 5}
true_sbr <- logbook_truth(sim, "Pagellus bogaraveo")
plot_index(fit_sbr, true = true_sbr)
plot_influence(fit_sbr, "DPC+S")
```

The same model fitted to all trips, for comparison:

```{r sbr-all, fig.height = 4}
fit_sbr_all <- fit_cpue(x, species = "Pagellus bogaraveo", models = "DPC+S",
                        vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
compare_indices(list(`DPC+S, demersal trips` = list(fit = fit_sbr, model = "DPC+S"),
                     `DPC+S, all trips` = list(fit = fit_sbr_all, model = "DPC+S")),
                true_sbr)
```

## Check the error distribution: predictive check

Residual plots check each observation against its own predicted
distribution. A predictive check asks a complementary question: **does the
fitted error distribution reproduce the data as a whole**: the share of
zeros, the upper tail and the shape of the positive catches?

`ppc_cpue()` simulates `n_sim` replicate data sets from each fitted model:
for every trip the expected CPUE is computed (with coefficients drawn from
their approximate posterior, so parameter uncertainty is included) and a new
value is drawn from the fitted Tweedie distribution. Each replicate is
summarised like the observed data, and the spread across the replicates gives
a 95% envelope.

```{r sbr-ppc}
pp_sbr <- ppc_cpue(fit_sbr, models = c("Base", "DPC+S"), n_sim = 50)
pp_sbr
```

```{r sbr-ppc-plots, fig.height = 5}
pp_sbr$plots$distribution
pp_sbr$plots$zeros
pp_sbr$plots$tails
```

> **Guidelines: reading a predictive check**
>
> * **Overall zeros** (in the panel titles of the distribution plot):
>   observed outside the simulated range means the error model gets the
>   zeros wrong. A Poisson-type or lognormal-type error with an added
>   constant typically predicts too few zeros.
> * **Zeros by year**: the most informative plot. The year effect fixes the
>   mean, not the zeros: a model without targeting covariates gives every trip
>   in a year the same expected catch and misses the zeros in years when much
>   of the fleet fished other habitats. A good targeting term brings the
>   observed zeros inside the envelope.
> * **Upper quantiles**: observed below the envelope means the tail of the
>   model is too heavy (e.g. a negative binomial or a lognormal with large
>   variance), above means too light.
> * **Histogram** (distribution plot): the observed histogram of CPUE,
>   with the zeros as the leftmost bar, against the predictive distribution
>   (points with 95% ranges). Bars outside the ranges show where the error
>   model fails: too many observed zeros next to too few small catches, or
>   a peak where the model is flat, point to the wrong distribution or
>   power. The default fourth-root scale keeps zero next to the small
>   catches; `scale = "log"` shows the shape of the positive catches best.
> * The pooled check can hide errors that cancel across years, so look at
>   the by-year plots (or `by = "FT"`, `by = "month"`).
> * `tail_prob` is the share of replicates at least as large as the observed
>   value; values near 0 or 1 flag misfit.

# Conger (reef at all depths, two gears)

Conger lives on reefs over a wide depth range and is caught both by the reef
handline and by the bottom longline. The longline is closed deeper than
300 m from 2016, which changes how conger is caught.

## Indicator vessels

Many vessels catch conger only occasionally. An indicator fleet keeps the
vessels that fish its habitat regularly. `vessel_summary()` shows, for every
vessel, how often and in how many years it caught conger.

```{r conger-vessels}
vs <- vessel_summary(x0, target = "Conger conger")
head(vs, 10)
```

```{r conger-select}
xc <- select_vessels(x0, min_years = 5, min_records = 10,
                     target = "Conger conger", min_years_target = 5,
                     min_share_target = 0.25)
table(attr(xc, "vessels")$selected)
```

Since the data are simulated, we can see which vessel types the rules kept:

```{r conger-profile, fig.height = 4}
type <- tapply(sim$trips$vessel_type, sprintf("V%02d", sim$trips$vessel),
               function(z) z[1])
sel <- attr(xc, "vessels")
table(type = type[sel$vessel], selected = sel$selected)
groups <- list(demersal = demersal, pelagic = pelagic)
plot_vessel_profile(x0, groups = groups,
                    by = setNames(ifelse(sel$selected, "selected", "not selected"),
                                  sel$vessel))
```

> **Guidelines: indicator vessels**
>
> * Typical rules: active in at least `min_years` years with at least
>   `min_records` records each; caught the target in at least
>   `min_years_target` years; and in at least `min_share_target` of the
>   trips. Report the rules and the number of vessels kept.
> * Vessel rules act on whole vessels, so they do not change with a vessel's
>   targeting from trip to trip; combine them with `select_tactics()` or
>   `stephens_maccall()` for selection at the trip level.
> * Rules on the target species select vessels by their catches of it.
>   Vessels that stopped catching the target because it declined can be
>   dropped; prefer rules on years active and on the share of trips, and
>   compare with the index of all vessels.

Targeting covariates are computed **after** the last selection, then the
pelagic tactics are removed as for seabream:

```{r conger-targeting}
xc <- add_targeting(xc)
xc <- select_tactics(xc, species = demersal, min_share = 0.5)
tactic_table(xc)
```

## Standardise and choose the error distribution

Tweedie and delta-lognormal models are fitted with the same terms.

```{r conger-fit}
fit_con <- fit_cpue(xc, species = "Conger conger",
                    models = c("Base", "Base+S", "Cluster+S", "DPC+S"),
                    vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
fit_con_dl <- fit_cpue(xc, species = "Conger conger", models = "DPC+S",
                       family = "delta_lognormal", vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40,
                       engine = "bam")
cpue_diagnostics(fit_con)
```

```{r conger-index, fig.height = 5}
true_con <- logbook_truth(sim, "Conger conger")
plot_index(fit_con, true = true_con)
```

AIC cannot compare a Tweedie with a delta model, but a predictive check
can:

```{r conger-ppc, fig.height = 5}
pp_tw <- ppc_cpue(fit_con, models = "DPC+S")
pp_dl <- ppc_cpue(fit_con_dl, models = "DPC+S")
rbind(data.frame(family = "Tweedie", pp_tw$overall),
      data.frame(family = "delta-lognormal", pp_dl$overall))
pp_tw$plots$distribution
pp_dl$plots$distribution
pp_tw$plots$tails
pp_dl$plots$tails
```

Indices of the indicator fleet with both families, and of all vessels:

```{r conger-compare, fig.height = 4}
xa <- select_tactics(add_targeting(x0), species = demersal, min_share = 0.5)
fit_con_all <- fit_cpue(xa, species = "Conger conger", models = "DPC+S",
                        vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
compare_indices(list(`Tweedie, indicator vessels` = list(fit = fit_con, model = "DPC+S"),
                     `delta-lognormal, indicator vessels` = list(fit = fit_con_dl,
                                                                model = "DPC+S"),
                     `Tweedie, all vessels` = list(fit = fit_con_all, model = "DPC+S")),
                true_con)
```

> **Guidelines: error distribution**
>
> * Tweedie models zeros and positive catches with one mean; a delta model
>   lets the probability of a positive catch and the positive catch rate
>   change independently (e.g. when a closure changes where a gear can fish).
> * Choose with predictive checks (zeros, tails, shape) and residuals, not
>   with AIC across families.
> * If both fit equally well, prefer the simpler model and report the other
>   as a sensitivity.

# Dolphinfish (seasonal pelagic migrant)

Dolphinfish is caught by trolling and is only present in summer and autumn.
Its price booms in 2008-2015, when much of the fleet switches to pelagic
fishing.

## Keep the pelagic trips

```{r dol-select}
xp <- select_tactics(x, species = pelagic, min_share = 0.5)
tactic_table(xp)
plot_biplot(xp)
```

Within the pelagic trips, the PCs should now separate offshore species
(albacore, dolphinfish) from coastal ones (amberjack, mackerel); check the
loadings.

## Standardise with a seasonal term

Month enters as a cyclic smoother in every model except `Base`.

```{r dol-fit}
fit_dol <- fit_cpue(xp, species = "Coryphaena hippurus",
                    models = c("Base", "Covariates", "Cluster+S", "DPC+S"),
                    terms = 's(month, bs = "cc", k = 6)',
                    knots = list(month = c(0.5, 12.5)),
                    vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
cpue_diagnostics(fit_dol)
```

```{r dol-index, fig.height = 5}
plot_index(fit_dol, true = logbook_truth(sim, "Coryphaena hippurus"))
plot_effects(fit_dol, "DPC+S")$numeric
```

## Predictive check by month and by year

For a migrant, the share of zeros changes strongly over the year. A model
without the seasonal term predicts the same share of zeros in every month:

```{r dol-ppc, fig.height = 5}
pp_dol_m <- ppc_cpue(fit_dol, models = c("Base", "DPC+S"), by = "month")
pp_dol_m$plots$zeros
pp_dol_y <- ppc_cpue(fit_dol, models = c("Base", "DPC+S"), by = "year")
pp_dol_y$plots$zeros
pp_dol_y$plots$tails
```

```{r dol-vessels, fig.height = 4}
plot_vessel_effects(fit_dol, "DPC+S")
```

> **Guidelines: seasonal species**
>
> * Include the season (cyclic smoother) in all models except `Base`; check
>   the zeros by month with `ppc_cpue(..., by = "month")`.
> * Keep only the trips that could catch the species (here the pelagic
>   tactics); outside the season or the habitat, zeros carry no information
>   on abundance.
> * Seasonal availability can shift between years with temperature; a
>   `month x year` interaction or a temperature covariate may be needed in
>   real data.

# Summary

| Step | Blackspot seabream | Conger | Dolphinfish |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trip selection | demersal tactics (`select_tactics`) | demersal tactics | pelagic tactics |
| Vessel selection | all vessels | indicator vessels (`select_vessels` with target rules) | all vessels |
| Targeting covariates | PCA of demersal trips | PCA of demersal trips of indicator vessels | PCA of pelagic trips |
| Extra terms | space, vessel | space, vessel | month (cyclic), space, vessel |
| Error distribution | Tweedie | Tweedie vs delta-lognormal (predictive check) | Tweedie |
| Key diagnostic | zeros by year | tails and shape by family | zeros by month and year |

# Things to try

* `logbook_settings()` lists every setting; see *Setting up the logbook
  simulator* for what each does. Change the prices, the closure, the share of
  two-set trips (`logbook$two_sets`) and how often they switch tactic
  (`logbook$switch_tactic`), the reef patches (`reef_share`, `reef_scale`), or
  the loyalty of specialists (`loyalty`), and see how each affects the
  targeting covariates and the indices.
* Compare `n_pc` and the number of clusters, and the species set
  (`select_species(..., pool_other = TRUE)`).
* Compare `select_tactics()` with `stephens_maccall()` for seabream.
* Give the species diverging trends (`B_start`, `r`) and check whether the
  PCs start absorbing them.
